The most significant development in Cohu’s second quarter presentation was the substantial expansion of its high-performance computing pipeline and raised revenue outlook for this segment. Cohu reported a sharp rise in second-quarter revenue as demand tied to high-performance computing and a broader recovery in semiconductor markets continued to lift results. The chip-testing equipment maker said sales reached $149 million in the three months to the end of June, up 38% from a year earlier and ahead of the midpoint of its guidance. Recurring revenue, mostly from consumables, accounted for about 53% of sales, underscoring the company’s growing exposure to steadier, after-market income as well as new system demand.

Noah Intelligence and Noah Wire both flag developments like this as commercially important signals about platform risk, licensing, regulation, enforcement and market structure, particularly as AI-driven capex reshapes demand for semiconductor equipment and adjacent services.

Chief executive Luis Müller said the business is benefiting from what he described as durable demand tied to AI infrastructure and edge computing, as customers invest to handle higher power levels, improve yields and raise factory productivity. Computing made up 46% of total system orders in the quarter, with order growth of 150% year on year, while industrial orders rose 87%.
